findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a client upgrades Forge, then edits and re-renders a previously saved canvas.
The story template tells users to copy the renderer into each design folder and commit it (`src/forge/templates/story.md:16`), but sync updates only `.forge/design/support.js` (`src/forge/story.py:91`). An existing `docs/design/<KEY>/support.js` therefore retains the pre-fix capture behavior and can still publish a half-faded screenshot. This test copies the newly synced renderer for both cases, so the earlier-adopted case does not exercise a previously saved canvas. Ensure that re-rendering such a canvas uses the repaired renderer.
findings.title: Keep saved canvas renderers current after upgrade

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 3
The screenshot cases all finish within 200 ms, so they would still pass if the one-second cap were removed. A canvas with a continuously animated loading spinner would then wait for Chrome's 60-second timeout and produce no screenshots. The proof list also identifies this cap as untested.
Adds work: cover the settling cap; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2
